title: Memory signal correlator hotpatch and telemetry for cross-env GPU OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported intermittent GPU OOM crashes and silent KV-cache corruption during long-lived sessions. Root cause hypothesis is an interaction between slow KV index compaction + fragmented slab allocator under certain request size distributions. This ticket implements a lightweight 'memory signal correlator' runtime hotpatch that (1) surfaces higher-fidelity signals to our telemetry pipeline tying allocations, KV mutations, and slab activity to OOM windows, (2) adds a conservative in-process prefix-eviction heuristic to bound active KV working set under pressure, and (3) ships a narrow allocator patch that reduces worst-case slab churn for sequences > 8k tokens.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Correlator events appear in the telemetry pipeline with request/session tags and stack-ids for at least 95% of observed OOM windows in canaries; 2) Canary clusters (hosted/DED-small) show no OOM regressions and at least 40% reduction in tail memory spikes for synthetic long-session workload; 3) Prefix-eviction toggled on in canaries caps memory growth and does not increase median latency >5%; 4) Hotpatch produced, reviewed, and applied with documented rollback path.
notes: This work is intended to be low-risk but decisive: correlate first, then apply conservative mitigations. The correlator is also useful long-term for postmortems and automated regression detection.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after triage call with support, engineering, and SRE. Affected customers: ACME (hosted), HealthSys (dedicated), FinanceCo (private). Initial stack traces show slab allocator saturation followed by KV index mutation activity within 30s of OOM.

2025-02-19 - Carlos Nguyen: Reproduced high tail memory growth locally using long-session generator (seq lengths skewed to 12k tokens, concurrent sessions 120). Confirmed KV compaction churn correlates with allocator spikes. Starting correlate+eviction patch branch.

2025-02-20 - Marta Ivanov (SRE): Deployed memory signal correlator binary to canary-hosted and canary-dedicated clusters behind feature flag. Telemetry forwarding validated — events arriving in tracing with session_id and request_id tags.

2025-02-21 - Carlos Nguyen: Implemented prefix-eviction heuristic: evict oldest 10% of inactive prefixes when slab pressure crosses high-water mark (configurable). Local benchmarks show 3.8% median latency increase under worst-case synthetic workload.

2025-02-22 - Design review (Liu Chen): UX for runtime flagging and per-tenant controls documented. Decision: expose toggle in Console as 'kv_safe_eviction' with default OFF for existing tenants; enable for canaries & impacted customers.

2025-02-23 - QA (Elena Ruiz): Integration tests created: long-session soak for 6 hours against canary clusters, monitor for KV inconsistency checksum drift. Early results: no corruption observed; some requests retried due to eviction-induced misses (expected).
2025-02-24 - Carlos Nguyen: Opened PR #1342. Requesting two code reviews (memory allocator owner + kvcache owner). Included microbenchmarks and rollback script (reuse previous allocator binary).

2025-02-25 - Engineering lead (Jonas Becker): Prioritized hotpatch roll with staged rollout plan. Post-deploy will run extended canary for 48h and enable console alerting for correlator event rate > baseline.

2025-02-25 - Customer success (Priya Singh): Drafted comms for impacted customers describing mitigation, temporary memory cap, and timeline for permanent fix. Asked to coordinate maintenance window for Private installs.
implementation_plan: 1) Merge correlator + eviction + allocator patch to runtime-1.19-hotfix branch (PR #1342). 2) Build artifacts and smoke-test in CI. 3) Deploy to canary-hosted (low-traffic) and canary-dedicated (DED-small) behind feature flag. 4) Monitor for 48h: Grafana dashboards + correlator metrics + error budget. 5) If stable, enable for impacted tenants and schedule larger Dedicated rollout. 6) For Private customers, provide advisory + optional patch bundle and upgrade playbook.
rollback_plan: Revert feature flag and deploy previous runtime binary (runtime-1.18 stable). Rollback script included in PR. If memory regressions continue after rollback, escalate to SRE and pause deployments.
tests: - Unit tests for correlator event generation and tag propagation. - Integration test: end-to-end telemetry pipeline (runtime->tenant-trace->grafana). - Soak test: 6hr long-session for canaries. - Consistency test: KV checksum before/after compaction cycles.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Prefix eviction may increase cache misses and latency for some workloads. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, canary first, and per-tenant toggle. Risk: Correlator overhead adds CPU; mitigated by sampling (1 in N) and adaptive backoff. Risk: Private upgrade coordination — CS to schedule windows and provide rollback bundle.
owner_notes: Primary owners: Carlos (implementation), Marta (canary ops), Aisha (customer comms). Coordinate with Security if correlator includes any PII — events currently only tag session_id/request_id (opaque).
